The first path links (-)-beta-Curcumene to Serine-protein kinase ATM, which is then targeted by (2S,3R,4S,5S,6R)-2-[2,6-dimethoxy-4-[3-(3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl)-1,3,3a,4,6,6a-hexahydrofuro[3,4-c]furan-6-yl]phenoxy]-6-(hydroxymethyl)oxane-3,4,5-triol, which ultimately targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The second path connects (-)-beta-Curcumene to Asialoglycoprotein receptor 2, which is targeted by 3-Hydroxymollugin, which also targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. These findings suggest that (-)-beta-Curcumene may act as a modulator of the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 through different molecular mechanisms, potentially influencing its function in transporting organic anions. The evidence is consistent with the possibility of a broader biological role for (-)-beta-Curcumene in regulating transporter activity, though the exact mechanism remains to be fully elucidated.
